Six Pulls

Every point's place is one formula: x = pull(+x) − pull(−x), and the same for y and z. No steps, no cap, no springs, no spacing. Seven graphs, each a different set of six pulls, scored on lines they never saw. A new page beside the old ones: 16.4, 16.3.

Where each thing lives

Nothing on this page is in the brain. The brain's SQLite tables (v1 and v16) hold no x, y or z for any gate. The words and lines are your relation map of 2026-10-08 (27,606 spellings, one point per spelling as v16 has one gate per word) and Open English WordNet 2025. A test I ran in Python computed each word's six pulls; this page computes x, y, z from them with the formula above and draws them. There is no step, no cap, no spring, no spacing and no rest length: a point sits where its pulls put it, words with equal pulls sit on the same point, and a word with no pull sits at 0,0,0.

How a graph was scored

Your map's lines were split by a hash of the pair: 70% to build the pulls, 15% to choose among graphs, 15% held back. For each kind of line a formula is fitted on build lines: start at A, get a point. Then on held-back lines: how many words sit closer to that point than B really does. That share is the rank share: 0 means B is the closest word of all 27,606, 0.5 means chance.

Formulas tried for every kind: same place, shift by a fixed step, flip one, two or three axes then shift (the swap), the flip through origin, scale each axis, any linear map. The one that did best on the choose lines is shown; the scores are from the held-back lines.

Controls: the same graph with places shuffled among words (should be 0.5), and the first graph's six pulls each shuffled across words. A kind counts as pointed out when its rank share is under 0.25, the real word is among the 10 nearest at least 0.3% of the time (10× chance), and the shuffled control stays at 0.45 or more. My predictions were written down before any graph was scored.

No graph met the bar I set before scoring (7 of 9 map kinds and 3 of 5 WordNet kinds). The places fitted straight to the lines came closest (6 of 9), so 3D itself is not what stops it. That fitted graph is not a true ceiling: it beats the pull formulas on alike, opposite, is and has, and loses on past, singular and stem.

Suffix and prefix lines score near 0 in most graphs, but they never count as pointed out. Even with places shuffled they score 0.22 to 0.36, because nearly all of them end at a few affix words ("ed", "s", "un"); a formula that always points at the same spot finds those.

The six named pulls that won

Out of 106 measured pulls (class, tense, number, modifiers, 45 WordNet topics, source, depth, and the reach of each word you listed), the search kept: +x in WordNet, −x reach of "write"; +y noun, −y adjective; +z adverb share, −z reach of "hear". These are pulls of class and of how connected a word is. None of them is tense, mood, memory, correct or incorrect. The reach pulls mostly measure how near a word is to the middle of your map's lines, whichever word they start from: two reach pulls rank words alike (rank correlation 0.63, median of all pairs).

The x axis mostly cancels: 20,187 words are pulled both by +x and by −x above 0.1. That is your "x,−x,y,z" bisect: +x and −x cancel and the point drops onto the y,z diagonal. In x, y, z that information is gone; only the six numbers keep it.

Opposite

In every graph except the signed one, the best formula for opposite is "same place": opposites sit near each other, because they share almost everything except one thing. Through origin (B = −A) scores 0.49 to 0.89: chance or worse. On most axes opposite pairs sit on the same side of 0 more often than chance.

The signed graph is built with opposite lines pushing apart. There "through origin" wins (0.216), and 56 to 73% of opposite pairs sit on both sides of 0 (depending on the axis), against 41 to 49% by chance. Everything else in that graph is weak.

Diagonal pulls

On top of the six named pulls, I tried every unused pull along each of the 20 diagonals and kept a pull only while it helped. Three were kept: reach of "modifier" on +x,−y,+z; "is a part" on −x,−y,+z; "is an affix" on −x,+y,−z. All three sit on three-axis diagonals. On held-back lines they moved the mean from 0.102 to 0.085, and WordNet kinds pointed out from 1 to 3.

Do they relate to their main axes? Not in one way. Reach of "modifier" tracks the −x and −z pulls (correlation 0.64 and 0.43), the ends opposite its own diagonal. "Is a part" relates to no axis. "Is an affix" leans slightly to its own three ends (0.08 against 0.01).

Which of the 26 directions hold words: in the fitted graph and the actions graph, all 26. In your named pulls, 8 directions hold no word, and most words sit nearest a two-axis diagonal (18,353), because class pulls are mostly 0 or 1.

Meaning checks

  • Distance from 0,0,0 follows how specific a word is (how many WordNet kinds sit above it): rank correlation 0.41 in your named pulls, 0.53 in the found six, 0.36 in the fitted graph, about 0 in the others. General words sit nearer the origin.
  • The fourteen actions sit close together in most graphs: 0.52× the spread of random words in your named pulls, 0.06× in the found six. Only the actions graph spreads them (3.2×), because each action is a pull there.
  • The word "origin" never lands at 0,0,0. In your named pulls it sits at 47.9, 100.0, −10.9, with nouns.

Where my predictions were wrong

  • I expected the found pulls (eigenvectors) to beat your named pulls. The reverse: named 0.102, eigenvectors 0.390 and 0.269. The eigenvectors land on a few tight word groups (greetings, fake/real, pride/humility) and leave most words near 0.
  • I expected diagonal pulls to help less than 10%. They helped 17%.
  • I expected the fourteen actions to sit apart in the found graphs (0.9). They cluster (0.53 and 0.06).
  • I expected the fitted placement to meet my bar. It did not (6 of 9).

Not tested

Memory, state, correct and incorrect as rows in the brain: the v16 brain holds one or two memory rows after a line, too few to test a pull. Mood, situation, perspective and context have no source that gives each word a value; I could only test the reach of those words through your map's lines. SQL and sources: 25 of the 40 SQL words and 1 of the 7 source names are in your map; their places are on the stage, but no SQL pull was tested.
